title: Core B: Biostatistics and Bioinformatics
text: Summary/Abstract The Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core (Core B) facility will provide study design, pipeline development, data management, and computational support for all SPORE in Leukemia investigators and projects. The Biostatistics component of the Core will perform consultation and collaboration on all aspects of statistical study design, database development, quality control, data analysis and interpretation. The Bioinformatics component of the Core will perform consultation and collaboration on all aspects of genomics and bioinformatics study design, pipeline development, multi-omics data integration, visualization, interpretation and genomic data sharing through controlled access systems. Core B will provide bioinformatics and biostatistics collaborations for SPORE projects, Developmental Research Program (DRP) studies, and other Cores to ensure that robust statistical methods and robust reproducible omics analyses are available to support SPORE investigators. Core B will also provide bioinformatics and biostatistical support and training to junior investigators through the Career Enhancement Program (CEP). The Biostatistics and Bioinformatics components of Core B will work together closely to ensure their efforts are integrated and complementary.

title: Hispanic Firearm Suicide Decedents: Identifying Circumstances and Typologies with National Violent Death Reporting System Data
text:
Modified Public Health Relevance

Nearly 1 in 2 suicide deaths among Hispanic adults involves a firearm, the most lethal suicide method. However, there are critical gaps in characterizing firearm suicide deaths and identifying opportunities for preventing firearm suicide. Identifying the circumstances preceding firearm suicides among Hispanic adults and generating new information on different profiles of Hispanic adult firearm suicide decedents are critical steps toward interventions for all Americans.

title: Population-genetic methods for inferring recent histories and targets of selection in the biobank era
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
A fundamental goal of evolutionary and biomedical studies of human genomes is to determine the genetic basis
of human traits and diseases. The scale of biobank datasets, generated by huge investments from entities
around the world (including the NIH), is revealing the complex interaction between environments, recent
migrations, and relatedness that confound our understanding of the genetic basis of human traits. The proposed
research will develop methods to address these challenges, bringing new insight into the evolutionary forces that
shape human genetic and phenotypic variation.

title: Targeting Trained Immunity in Trauma-Induced Immune Dysregulation
text:
Traumatic injuries from burns, blasts, or major surgery disrupts normal immune system functions, which can
lead to the development of life-threatening infections and prolonged critical illnesses. Targeted
immunotherapies for traumatic injuries to restore immune system function have not yet been developed and
are urgently needed. This project studies the scientific processes involved in using specific natural
immunostimulatory DNA as a novel treatment approach to enhance immune system health in immune
compromised trauma patients that are at risk of dying from complications of their injuries.

title: Noninvasive Monitoring of Hepatic Glutathione Depletion Through Blood Test
text:
Glutathione (GSH) is the master antioxidant in the body and mainly produced in hepatocytes and
depletion of hepatic glutathione has found to strongly correlate with an increased susceptibility to oxidative stress
and high risk of many diseases ranging from liver injuries to immunodeficiency, Parkinson’s disease and
infectious diseases; however, unlike those conventional serum markers, hepatic glutathione depletion cannot be
readily monitored through blood testing. The objective of this proposal is to develop an innovation
nanotechnology that empower blood test to be a simple and rapid tool for noninvasive and consecutive
monitoring of hepatic GSH depletion. The success will allow this crucial pathophysiological process to be readily
monitored in the clinics and serve as an earlier indicator for liver injuries and many other oxidative-stress related
diseases.

title: BSL3 Drug Screening Core
text: (Core 1) High-throughput screening (HTS) has become the cornerstone of modern drug discovery both in Industry and Academia, allowing for the implementation of large-scale screening campaigns where thousands of compounds can be tested in search for novel drugs against a given disease. However, the overwhelming majority of existing HTS facilities and specialized equipment are set up in laboratories under low biosafety level (BSL) conditions. This makes it impossible to implement this approach for highly pathogenic microorganisms, such as Coccidioides spp., since work with these pathogens needs to be conducted inside high level biocontainment facilities. Thus, the overarching goal of this Drug Screening Core is to establish unique capabilities within BSL-3 conditions, which will allow for the implementation of fast, efficient and economical HTS techniques for large-scale screening of chemical libraries for the identification of novel anti-coccidioidal agents. More specifically, we propose to: i) develop low- and high-density microtiter plate-based models for Coccidioides spp. susceptibility testing amenable to HTS inside our BSL-3 facility, and ii) to fully develop a novel fungal cytological profiling (FCP) system based on imaging flow cytometry (IFC), and adapt it for drug screening and to determine the mode of action of novel drugs. Within the CCRC, this Core will support the screening and fungal cytological profiling activities in Project 1, provide services for down-selection of top candidates for in vivo evaluation in Project 2, and support Project 3 activities examining immunotherapeutic efficacy of antifungal drugs and vaccine candidates. Furthermore, once fully established, the technical capabilities of this Core will be provided to the Coccidioides scientific community at large, as well as to others in the field of Medical Mycology, and potentially other investigators working with BSL-3 organisms.

title: Combined Imaging and RNA Analyses to Predict Head and Neck Cancer Recurrence
text:
The major goal of this study is to develop a comprehensive and robust computational model for early prediction
of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) treatment failures leading to tumor recurrence. The
biomarker signature will form a solid basis for individualized care of HNSCC patients. Moreover, our work is
expected to discover the correlations among multimodal data, leading to dynamic patient stratification to support
adaptive treatment strategies.

title: Increasing Access, Diagnostic Yield, and Efficiency in Clinical Evaluations of Rare Disorders
text: The University of Alabama at Birmingham UAB Undiagnosed Diseases Program (UAB UDP) provides diagnostic assessments for children and adults with chronic undiagnosed conditions. It is currently a Diagnostic Center of Excellence in the Undiagnosed Diseases Network (UDN). This proposal describes numerous innovations to the UAB UDP, including increased use of telemedicine and a “genome-first” diagnostic approach, the inclusion of basic scientists in a set of diagnostic teams, collaboration with a federally qualified health center, and incorporation of a set of bioinformatic and AI-powered tools, all aimed to increase patient access, as well as to improve diagnostic success rates and turnaround times.

title: Dynamics of Notch Signaling
text:
Signal transduction pathways underlie the very basis of life and are often critical targets for disease therapeutics.
This work focuses on the molecular events of Notch signaling, which exerts a critical influence on cell
differentiation in mammals and its misregulation is associated with diverse diseases, including the pathogenesis
of many human cancers. This work will use two emerging technologies, proximity labeling and lattice light sheet
microscopy, to provide unprecedented resolution in both space and time of the fundamental events required for
transmission of physiologic Notch signals in living cells.

title: UC Davis IGA Innovation Center
text:
Gene editing has the potential to improve the resilience, health and productivity of animals raised
for food and thus the sustainability of a safe and healthy food supply. We propose to establish an
Innovation Center focused on intentional genomic alterations (IGA) to advance the use of gene
editing technologies in food animals while contributing data to support a science-based regulatory
approach to the regulation of IGAs. The information gained through this Cooperative Agreement
will lead to the safe implementation of gene editing in animals raised for food to ensure animal
health and productivity and thus food security and public health.

title: Accurate, low-cost, trackerless neuronavigation for transcranial magnetic stimulation
text:
Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) uses magnetic fields sent from a “wand” placed on the head to safely
treat brain disorders without drugs. However, existing TMS devices have limited ability to stimulate the brain
precisely and doing so requires expensive equipment and uncomfortable headgear. This project will develop a
cheaper and more comfortable tool to position precisely the TMS wand based on tracking of the patient’s face,
which could improve the patients’ experience and clinical outcome.

title: Atoh7 interacting proteins involved in retinal ganglion cell genesis
text:
This project aims to understand how Atoh7, a key regulator controlling the developmental genesis of retinal
ganglion cells, interacts with other protein partners to carry out its function. Retinal ganglion cells are a type of
neurons in the retina that are critical for vision and are implicated in multiple retinal diseases. The study will
lead to a better understanding of the developmental process and help develop therapeutic strategies to treat
relevant retinal diseases such as glaucoma.

title: Foundational Porcine Stem Cell and Genetic Tools to Enable Rigorous, Reproducible Generation of Large-Animal Models
text:
This project will generate genetic tools in pigs that allow scientists to study heart disease, diabetes, cancer,
and other chronic illnesses in ways that more closely mimic human biology. These resources will accelerate
the development of new treatments, improve testing of therapies before they reach patients, and ultimately
help reduce the burden of chronic disease on public health.

title: Characterization and treatment of an accelerated aging model of the olfactory epithelium
text:
Our sense of smell declines with age, with nearly the majority of all individuals above the age of 80 suffering
from some form of hyposmia or anosmia. Despite this huge patient population, no treatment for this exists, due
in large part to the lack of an effective preclinical model. This proposal, submitted by an early career
researcher, describes the successful creation of an efficient accelerated aging model of the olfactory
epithelium, proposes to fully characterize it in the context of normal human aging, test the hypothesis that true
respiratory metaplasia emerges during stem cell exhaustion, and finally, test two potential treatments for this
condition.

title: Clean Hands Accessible and Manageable for Patients (CHAMPs): A technology-based self-management intervention to improve patient hand hygiene and reduce hand contamination among older adults.
text:
This study proposes the novel use of a bedrail-affixed technology-based patient hand hygiene system with
verbal and visual reminders to improve hospitalized older adults’ self-management of their hand hygiene
practice, which in return reduces harmful germs found on hands that lead to infections.

title: Project 1: Targeting Neutrophils to Enhance ICI Efficacy in NSCLC
text:
Despite recent advances in lung cancer early detection and treatment, lung cancer remains the leading cause
of cancer death worldwide. Immune based therapies possess great potential to improve lung cancer survival
metrics though they still benefit too few patients for too short a period of time. The major goals of this project
are to develop an Immune Phenotype Classifier to readily detect lung cancers with myeloid cell infiltration and
to develop a therapeutic strategy that would render such tumors amenable to immune checkpoint inhibitor
therapy.

title: Social Isolation Re-Organizes Neural Dynamics Governing Mating
text:
Prolonged social isolation results in widespread, deleterious effects on the brain and behavior, and represents
one of the largest public health concerns facing humanity. One of the most striking impacts of isolation is its
ability to disrupt courtship behavior across species, yet, the brain circuits and neural dynamics underlying this
effect, and its impact on reproduction, are largely unknown. Combining in-depth behavioral analyses, acoustic
recordings, advanced computational approaches, cell-type specific functional manipulations, and in vivo
microendoscopic imaging of neural activity in male and female mice, we will close this gap in knowledge.

title: Citrate regulation in amelogenesis
text:
Public Health Relevance: Knowledge gained from the proposed project will provide critical information on the
roles of citrate in amelogenesis, particularly in understanding genetic and systemic factors contributing to
amelogenesis. Enamel possesses distinct characteristics from other mineralized tissues, and when
compromised, can lead to dental caries, weakened tooth structure, and in severe cases, tooth loss. Results
from this study will contribute knowledge toward developing new models to study enamel formation and
determining potential interventions to mitigate the progression of enamel disorders and potentially other
mineralized tissues.

title: Molecular Atlas of the Cardiac Intercalated Disc
text:
Ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac arrest are a major cause of mortality and morbidity, carrying great
economical and societal impact. Our research applies primarily to arrhythmias originating in the cardiac
intercalated disc and subject to the interplay between PKP2, Cx43 and intracellular calcium. We use modern
physiology, proteomics and microscopy methods to investigate the mechanisms underlying the onset of disease
at the molecular level and to design novel venues for therapy.

title: Pneumatically controlled RF coil design for multinuclear magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy
text:
The project aims to develop and evaluate an innovative RF coil incorporating pneumatically controlled capacitor
arrays for multinuclear MRI applications, specifically targeting metabolic MRI and MRS at an ultrahigh field
strength of 7 Tesla (7T). The anticipated outcomes of this research hold significant potential to revolutionize the
diagnosis and treatment of various diseases, including cancer, by providing insights into metabolic pathways
and enabling more precise and personalized medical interventions.
